about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice B): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Numbing Chilli Bean Tofu with Pork over Rice
recipes.summary: Silken tofu in a numbing chilli bean gravy with pork mince, served over rice.
steps: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Fry the pork in the oil over high heat for 4 minutes until browned and cooked through at 75°C, then add the doubanjiang, garlic, ginger and peppercorn and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the stock and soy sauce, add the tofu and simmer gently for 5 minutes until hot.
Stir the cornflour with a little water and add until the gravy thickens and turns glossy. Scatter with spring onion and serve over rice.
notes: Food safety: cook the pork mince to 75°C with no pink.

recipes.title: Cantonese Steamed Chicken with Ginger and Shiitake
recipes.summary: Tender chicken pieces steamed with shiitake and ginger, gluten free with tamari.
steps: Toss the chicken with the tamari, wine, sesame oil, cornflour, ginger and mushrooms.
Spread on a heatproof plate and steam over simmering water for 20 minutes until the chicken is opaque and reaches 75°C.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then serve the chicken and its juices over rice with spring onion.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout with no pink.

recipes.title: Honey Garlic Pork Rice Plates
recipes.summary: Sticky glazed pork slices with garlic and sesame over rice.
steps: Mix the honey, soy sauce and garlic.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, and steam the broccoli for 4 minutes until bright green.
Sear the pork in the oil for 4 minutes until browned, add the glaze and cook until sticky and the pork reaches 70°C.
Serve over rice with broccoli and sesame seed.
notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C with no pink remaining.

recipes.title: Tofu and Mushroom Vegan Lunch Pot
recipes.summary: Braised tofu and mushrooms with soy and ginger over rice, vegan.
steps: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Fry the tofu in the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then set aside.
Cook the mushrooms and ginger for 5 minutes until browned, then return the tofu with the soy sauce and 1/4 cup water and simmer until reduced.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onion and serve over rice.

recipes.title: Okinawan Sweet Potato Rice Pot
recipes.summary: Rice cooked with purple-fleshed style sweet potato and kombu, savoury and gently sweet.
steps: Rinse the rice and place in a pot with the water, kombu, soy sauce, mirin and potato.
Bring to the boil, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the rice is tender and the potato soft.
Rest, covered, for 10 minutes until fluffy, then stir and scatter with sesame seed.

recipes.title: Goya-Free Okinawan Pork and Tofu Champuru
recipes.summary: Stir-fried pork, firm tofu, cabbage and egg Okinawa style.
steps: Fry the pork in the oil 4 minutes until browned and cooked through to 70°C.
Add the cabbage and crumbled tofu and stir-fry for 4 minutes until wilted.
Pour in the beaten eggs and soy sauce and stir until set, then top with the bonito flakes.
notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C and cook the egg until set.

recipes.title: Hokkaido Butter Corn Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Sweet corn and butter over rice with soy and spring onion.
steps: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the corn 5 minutes until lightly golden.
Stir in the soy sauce and pepper, spoon over the rice and top with spring onion.

recipes.title: Salmon Teriyaki Tray Bake with Rice
recipes.summary: Glazed salmon with broccoli roasted together, served with rice.
steps: Toss the broccoli in the oil on a large tray and bake at 200°C for 8 minutes until beginning to colour.
Add the salmon brushed with the teriyaki sauce and bake 10 minutes until the salmon is opaque and flakes easily.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with sesame seed.
notes: Food safety: salmon is cooked when opaque and flaking, or 63°C.

recipes.title: Jeju Style Braised Pork and Radish Rice Pot
recipes.summary: Pork belly and radish simmered in soy and ginger until tender.
steps: Simmer the pork in water for 10 minutes and drain.
Return to the pot with the daikon, soy sauce, sugar, ginger, garlic and fresh water.
Cover and simmer 45 minutes until the pork is tender and has passed 70°C inside.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with spring onion.
notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C.

recipes.title: Dakgalbi Spicy Chicken Rice Plates
recipes.summary: Chicken thigh with gochujang, sweet potato and cabbage stir-fried together.
steps: Mix the gochujang, soy, honey and garlic and coat the chicken.
Fry the sweet potato in the oil 6 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the chicken and cabbage and cook 10 minutes until the chicken reaches 75°C and the sweet potato is tender.
Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve alongside.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout.

recipes.title: Gochujang Tofu Lunch Wraps
recipes.summary: Crisp tofu with gochujang glaze, kimchi and cucumber in flour tortillas, vegan.
steps: Fry the tofu in the oil 7 minutes until golden.
Toss with gochujang and maple syrup for 1 minute until sticky.
Warm the tortillas until pliable and fill with tofu, kimchi and cucumber.

recipes.title: Isan Grilled Chicken with Sticky Rice
recipes.summary: Marinated grilled chicken thighs with lemongrass and garlic over sticky rice, gluten free.
steps: Blend the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, sugar, tamari and pepper and coat the chicken.
Soak the rice 30 minutes, then steam 25 minutes until tender and chewy.
Grill the chicken 12 minutes each side until charred and 75°C.
Serve with the sticky rice.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C throughout.
Plus 1 hour marinating.

recipes.title: Cashew Tofu with Capsicum over Jasmine Rice
recipes.summary: Crisp tofu, capsicum and cashews in a sweet-savoury sauce, vegan.
steps: Cook the rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Fry the tofu in the oil 6 minutes until golden, add garlic and capsicum and cook until crisp-tender.
Add the soy, sugar and cashews and toss until glossy.
Spoon the glossy tofu and cashews over the rice and serve straight away.

recipes.title: Hue Style Lemongrass Beef Noodle Bowls
recipes.summary: Beef strips with lemongrass, chilli and noodles.
steps: Cook the vermicelli per the packet until tender and drain.
Marinate the beef in lemongrass, chilli, fish sauce, sugar.
Sear in the oil 2 minutes until browned and 63°C inside.
Serve over noodles with sprouts and mint.
notes: Food safety: cook beef to at least 63°C.
Plus 20 minutes marinating.

recipes.title: Ginger Tofu Banh Mi Baguettes
recipes.summary: Crisp ginger soy tofu in baguette with pickled carrot, vegan.
steps: Marinate the tofu in soy and ginger.
Fry in the oil until golden, 3 minutes a side.
Toss the carrot in the vinegar until softened.
Fill the baguette with tofu, carrot, cucumber and coriander.

recipes.title: Javanese Sweet Soy Chicken Rice Plates
recipes.summary: Chicken thigh braised in kecap manis and garlic.
steps: Fry shallot, garlic and ginger in oil 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add chicken and brown 5 minutes.
Add kecap manis and 1/2 cup water, cover and simmer 15 minutes until chicken reaches 75°C.
Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve with cucumber.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C.

recipes.title: Sambal Egg Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Boiled eggs coated in sambal and tomato over rice.
steps: Boil the eggs for 8 minutes until firm, peel.
Fry garlic and tomato in oil 3 minutes until soft, add sambal.
Add eggs and coat for 2 minutes until sticky.
Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, serve together.
notes: Food safety: boil eggs until firm.

recipes.title: Sabah Style Fish Curry with Okra
recipes.summary: Tangy chilli fish curry with okra and tomato, gluten free.
steps: Fry onion, garlic and ginger in oil 5 minutes.
Add chilli powder, tomato, tamarind paste, and 1 cup water and simmer 8 minutes until thick.
Add okra and fish and simmer 6 minutes until fish is opaque and flakes.
Cook rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy and serve.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when opaque and flaking.

recipes.title: Malaysian Coconut Egg Breakfast Bowls
recipes.summary: Soft-boiled eggs with coconut rice and sambal.
steps: Cook the rice with the coconut milk and 1/2 cup water until tender and fluffy.
Boil the eggs for 6 minutes then cool and peel.
Serve rice topped with eggs, sambal, cucumber, peanuts.
notes: Food safety: use fresh eggs.

recipes.title: Kerala Style Coconut Prawn Stir-Fry
recipes.summary: Prawns with curry leaf, coconut and black pepper, gluten free.
steps: Heat the coconut oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the sliced onion with a pinch of salt and fry for 5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the curry leaf, turmeric and black pepper and cook for 30 seconds until the leaves crackle and the pan smells fragrant.
Add the prawns and toss over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, until they curl, turn pink and opaque, and the spices cling to the shells or flesh.
Sprinkle over the desiccated coconut and toss for 1 minute until it turns lightly golden and nutty. Taste and add salt if needed.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy, then fluff with a fork and serve the prawns over the top.
notes: Food safety: cook prawns until opaque and pink throughout, then eat straight away or chill within 1 hour and eat within 24 hours.
Tip: do not overcook the prawns or they turn rubbery; pull the pan off the heat as soon as they curl into a loose C shape.

recipes.title: Punjabi Chole Bhature-Style Chickpea Plates
recipes.summary: Spiced chickpeas with puffed fried breads, vegan.
steps: Mix the flour with 1 tsp salt in a bowl. Add the water and 1 tbsp of the oil and knead for 5 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic. Cover and rest.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the onions for 6 minutes, stirring, until deep golden brown.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste and garam masala and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chopped tomato and cook for 6 minutes until jammy and the oil separates at the edges.
Tip in the drained chickpeas with 1/2 cup water, mash a few against the pot and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick and glossy. Season with salt.

Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each into a 12cm oval. Heat the 1/4 cup oil in a deep pan to about 180°C (a scrap of dough should sizzle and rise at once). Fry each bread for 30 to 40 seconds, pressing gently, until puffed and golden on both sides.
Drain the breads on paper towel and serve hot with the chickpeas.
notes: Plus 20 minutes resting the dough.
Tip: roll the dough evenly so the breads puff; thin patches stay flat. Keep the oil hot between batches.
Food safety: take care with hot oil and never leave the pan unattended.

recipes.title: Mushroom Matar Lunch Curry with Roti
recipes.summary: Mushrooms and peas in a spiced tomato base, vegan.
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the onion with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste and garam masala and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the chopped tomato and cook for 5 minutes, mashing, until jammy.
Add the sliced mushrooms and 1/2 cup water. Cook for 5 minutes until the mushrooms release their liquid and shrink, then add the peas.
Simmer for 8 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Season with 1/2 tsp salt.
Warm each roti in a dry pan over medium heat for 30 seconds a side until soft and flecked with brown, and serve with the curry.
notes: Tip: do not wash mushrooms under water; wipe them so the sauce stays rich rather than watery.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Sri Lankan Black Pork Curry
recipes.summary: Dark roasted spice pork shoulder curry with tamarind, gluten free.
steps: Toast the curry powder, ground coriander and black pepper in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until a few shades darker and smoky-fragrant. Tip into a bowl.
Heat the oil in the same pot over medium-high heat. Brown the pork in two batches for 5 minutes each until deeply coloured on all sides, then set aside.
Add the sliced onion to the pot and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Stir in the crushed garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Return the pork with the roasted spices, tamarind paste, cinnamon stick, 1 tsp salt and 2 cups water. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 80 minutes, stirring now and then, until the pork is very tender (at least 70°C inside) and the sauce is dark, thick and clings to the meat.
Meanwhile cook 1 1/2 cups of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Remove the cinnamon stick, taste and adjust the salt, then serve the curry over the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook fresh pork to 70°C or above, refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot.
Tip: the dark colour comes from the long roast of the spices; stop before they turn bitter and black.
Storage: tastes better the next day; keeps 3 days in the fridge.

recipes.title: Sri Lankan Egg Roti Lunch Pockets
recipes.summary: Spiced egg and onion pockets in roti.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry the finely sliced onion and green chilli with a pinch of salt for 4 minutes until soft and translucent.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, pour into the pan and stir gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until just set and no longer runny.
Warm each roti in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side until soft. Spoon the egg onto one half, fold over into a pocket and serve warm.
notes: Food safety: cook the egg until set and eat promptly; do not keep the filling warm for long.
Tip: leave the chilli seeds out for a milder filling.

recipes.title: Berbere-Style Spiced Chicken Flatbread Rolls
recipes.summary: Spiced chicken stewed with eggs, rolled in flatbread.
steps: Cook the finely diced onion in a dry, wide pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly browned at the edges.
Add the butter, paprika and cumin with 1/2 tsp salt and stir for 1 minute until the butter melts and the spices smell fragrant.
Add the chicken and 1/2 cup water. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is cooked through (at least 75°C) and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile boil the eggs in simmering water for 9 minutes until firm, cool in cold water and peel. Halve them and warm through in the sauce for 2 minutes.
Warm the flatbread in a dry pan for 30 seconds a side until soft and pliable. Spoon the chicken and egg onto each, roll up tightly and serve.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C and boil eggs until firm; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: sweet paprika is used here, so the dish is warm rather than hot; add a pinch of chilli flakes for heat.

recipes.title: Kenyan Beef Samosa Plates
recipes.summary: Crisp beef mince triangles with tomato and cucumber.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook the finely chopped onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the mince and curry powder with 1/2 tsp salt.
Cook for 8 minutes, breaking up the mince, until browned and cooked through (at least 75°C) and the liquid has evaporated. Cool for 10 minutes.
Cut each wrapper in half. Place a spoonful of filling at one corner and fold over and over into a triangle, sealing the final edge with a dab of water.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Shallow-fry the samosas for 3 minutes a side, until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towel and serve with sliced tomato and cucumber.
notes: Food safety: cook beef mince to 75°C; cool the filling and refrigerate within 2 hours if not using straight away.
Tip: let the filling cool or the wrappers tear and turn soggy.
Make ahead: fold the samosas and chill for up to a day before frying.

recipes.title: Tanzanian Coconut Bean Stew
recipes.summary: Kidney beans in coconut milk and tomato, vegan, gluten free.
steps: Heat a splash of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the chopped onion and crushed garlic with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomato and curry powder and cook for 6 minutes, stirring, until the tomato breaks down into a thick paste.
Add the drained beans and coconut milk with 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer gently for 10 minutes, mashing a few beans against the pot, until the stew is thick and creamy.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy. Serve the stew over the rice.
notes: Tip: simmer rather than boil the coconut milk so it stays smooth.
Storage: keeps 4 days in the fridge; thin with a splash of water when reheating until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Maize Pap Bowls with Curried Tomato Onion
recipes.summary: Maize pap with spiced tomato and onion, vegan.
steps: Bring the water and 1/2 tsp salt to the boil in a heavy pot. Slowly pour in the polenta in a thin stream, whisking constantly until smooth and lump-free.
Reduce to low and cook for 15 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until the pap is thick, pulls from the sides and no grittiness remains.
Meanwhile heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the sliced onions with a pinch of salt for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the curry powder for 30 seconds, then add the chopped tomato and simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy.
Spoon the pap into bowls and top with the curried tomato onion while hot.
notes: Tip: pour the polenta in a thin stream; adding it quickly makes lumps.
Pap thickens as it cools, so serve at once.

recipes.title: Curried Apricot Chicken Skewers on Basmati
recipes.summary: Curried chicken skewers with apricot, gluten free.
steps: Soak 8 wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes (or use metal skewers). Toss the cubed chicken with the curry powder, apricot jam, oil and 1/2 tsp salt in a bowl until evenly coated.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers with the onion cut into wedges, leaving a little space between pieces.
Grill or barbecue on medium-high heat for 15 minutes, turning every few minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (at least 75°C) and charred at the edges.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry basmati rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Serve the skewers whole on top of the rice, or slide the chicken off the skewers into the rice.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C, use clean utensils for the cooked chicken and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Plus 30 minutes marinating is optional for a deeper flavour.
Tip: jam burns easily, so keep the heat medium and turn often.

recipes.title: Bunny Chow Bean Curry Loaf
recipes.summary: Hollowed bread filled with spiced bean curry, vegan.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the chopped onion with a pinch of salt for 6 minutes until golden, then stir in the curry powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomato, drained beans, cubed potato, 1 tsp salt and 1 cup water. Bring to a simmer and cook for 20 minutes, until the potato is tender and the curry is thick.
Cut the loaf in half, or slice off the top, and pull out the soft crumb to leave a 2cm thick shell.
Fill the bread with the hot curry and serve with the pulled-out bread for dipping.
notes: Tip: use a sturdy crusty loaf so the shell holds the curry without going soggy.
Traditionally eaten with your hands, so serve with plenty of napkins.

recipes.title: Ube-Free Purple Sweet Potato Rice Pancakes
recipes.summary: Rice flour pancakes with sweet potato mash.
steps: Peel the sweet potato, cut into chunks and boil for 12 minutes until very tender when pierced with a knife. Drain well and mash until completely smooth.
Whisk the mash with the rice flour, coconut milk, egg, sugar and a pinch of salt until you have a thick pourable batter. Rest for 5 minutes.
Heat a little coconut oil in a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Pour in 1/4 cup batter per pancake and cook for 3 minutes until bubbles appear and the underside is golden.
Flip and cook for 2 minutes until golden and cooked through. Repeat with the remaining oil and batter and serve warm.
notes: Food safety: cook until the centre is set and no longer wet; do not eat raw batter.
Tip: keep the heat low or the sugar in the batter will scorch before the middle sets.

recipes.title: Filipino Beef Tapa Lunch Wraps
recipes.summary: Garlic soy beef strips with tomato in tortillas.
steps: Toss the sliced beef with the soy sauce, crushed garlic and brown sugar and set aside for 20 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat. Sear the beef in 2 batches for 2 minutes a side until browned and caramelised at the edges and at least 63°C inside.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side until soft and pliable.
Slice the tomato and divide with the beef among the tortillas, then fold or roll up and serve warm.
notes: Plus 20 minutes marinating.
Food safety: cook beef to 63°C, keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat food and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: do not crowd the pan or the beef steams rather than sears.

recipes.title: Vegan Pancit Lunch Noodles
recipes.summary: Egg-free noodles stir-fried with cabbage, carrot and soy, vegan.
steps: Cook the noodles in boiling water for 4 minutes, or to packet directions, until tender but still springy. Drain and rinse briefly.
Heat the oil in a large wok over high heat. Stir-fry the crushed garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the julienned carrot and shredded cabbage.
Stir-fry for 4 minutes until crisp-tender and bright, with the edges just starting to colour.
Add the noodles and soy sauce and toss for 2 minutes until the noodles are glossy, evenly coloured and steaming hot.
Divide into bowls and serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.
notes: Tip: cut the vegetables thin and even so they cook in the same time as the noodles.
Storage: keeps 2 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Pacific Taro-Free Cassava Coconut Dumpling Plates
recipes.summary: Grated cassava flour dumplings in coconut milk, vegan, gluten free.
steps: Mix the cassava flour, coconut milk and salt in a bowl, kneading for 3 minutes until a soft, smooth dough forms that holds together. Add a splash of water if it cracks.
Shape into 12 balls the size of a walnut. Drop into a pot of simmering salted water and boil for 10 minutes, until they float and feel firm.
Drain well. Heat the coconut oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the dumplings for 3 minutes a side, until golden and lightly crisp.
Serve warm with sliced fresh tomato on the side, and a pinch of salt over the tomato.
notes: Tip: cassava flour absorbs a lot of liquid, so the dough should feel soft like play dough, not dry.
Storage: best eaten the same day.

recipes.title: Baked Lime Coconut Fish Rice Plates
recipes.summary: Fish baked in coconut milk with lime, gluten free.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Slice the onion and tomato and layer them in a baking dish with 1/2 tsp salt.
Lay the fish fillets on top. Pour over the coconut milk and the juice of the lime and season with a little more salt.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the fish turns opaque, flakes easily with a fork and reaches 63°C, and the sauce is bubbling.
Meanwhile cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Spoon the rice onto plates and top with fish and the coconut sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook fish until opaque and flaking (63°C); refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and eat within 24 hours.
Tip: pat the fish dry first so the sauce stays creamy.

recipes.title: Hawaiian Pineapple Tofu Rice Bowls
recipes.summary: Glazed tofu and pineapple over rice, vegan.
steps: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Pat the tofu dry. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the cubes for 6 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp on all sides.
Drain the pineapple and add to the pan with the teriyaki sauce. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce bubbles and turns sticky and glossy.
Spoon the tofu and pineapple over the rice and serve hot.
notes: Tip: pressing the tofu for 10 minutes before frying makes it crisper.
Storage: keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Samoan Style Coconut Chicken Parcels
recipes.summary: Chicken in coconut and spinach in foil, gluten free.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the chicken into large pieces and mix in a bowl with the coconut milk, thinly sliced onion, baby spinach and salt.
Cut four 35cm squares of foil. Divide the mixture among them and fold the edges over twice, pressing until sealed into airtight parcels with a little room for steam.
Place on a baking tray and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through (at least 75°C) and the juices are bubbling and creamy.
Rest the parcels for 5 minutes, then open carefully, away from your face, as the steam is very hot, and serve straight from the foil.
notes: Food safety: cook chicken to 75°C and check the thickest piece before serving.
Tip: serve with steamed rice or boiled cassava to soak up the coconut sauce.

recipes.title: Tongan Style Corned Beef Rice Pans
recipes.summary: Corned beef with onion and tomato over rice.
steps: Cook 1 cup of dry jasmine rice by your usual method until tender and fluffy.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry the sliced onion for 5 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the chopped tomato and cook for 4 minutes until softened and pulpy, then add the corned beef, breaking it up with a spoon.
Cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until the mixture is hot throughout and the tomato juices have reduced.
Spoon over the rice and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: reheat corned beef until steaming hot; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours.
Tip: canned corned beef is salty, so taste before adding any extra salt.
